run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: The incident evidence lives in Elasticsearch index app-262-prod-logs. That index holds exactly 5 documents in the authorized window, and the only failure records in it carry cluster=production-us-east-1: checkout-service logged a failed POST /api/checkout because the payment provider response timed out after 30s (Stripe-US) at 2026-11-22T07:49:48Z, payment-service logged an upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms at 08:49:47Z, and checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' at 09:19:47Z. In the same index, production-eu-west-1 checkout-service rows report 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' and 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at the same two sampling instants, so this is not a globally failing checkout build. The deepest failure the records name is the upstream call from payment-service to the external payment provider stripe-us, which is not represented by any object I can inspect, so the conclusion is partial: the chain checkout -> payment-service -> stripe-us is documented, the state inside stripe-us is unknown. The Kubernetes cluster readable in this Run is not the US prod cluster: its own Prometheus alert rule labels it cluster: opspilot-m1, it contains only otel-demo plus app-102, kube-* and lab namespaces (no app-262), its checkout/payment deployments are 1/1 ready on ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2 images with no stripe dependency, and its payment and checkout pods were completing transactions normally at 09:45-09:48Z. All 22 otel-demo pods in that cluster had terminated together at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exit code 255 (reason Unknown), a cluster-wide event I could not attribute to the checkout incident. Prometheus metric queries and all Jaeger trace queries returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE throughout this Run, so rates, error ratios and trace chains could not be measured, and no object in production-us-east-1 could be inspected.

claims.text: Index app-262-prod-logs is the only index present and contains 5 documents total; querying the whole authorized window (2026-11-21T09:49:56Z to 2026-11-22T09:49:56Z) returned all 5: three level=ERROR rows with cluster=production-us-east-1 and two level=INFO rows with cluster=production-eu-west-1.
checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T07:49:48Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'.
payment-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:49:47Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-1 logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:19:47Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'.

The two cluster=production-eu-west-1 rows in the same index are checkout-service level=INFO readings 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' (2026-11-22T08:49:47Z) and 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' (2026-11-22T09:19:47Z), i.e. the same service name in another cluster reported healthy at the same sampling instants as the US error rows.

The Elasticsearch schema that carries these rows has only the fields cluster, level, message, service and timestamp (keyword/text/date), and the index's documents span 2026-11-22T07:49:48Z to 2026-11-22T09:19:47Z; there is no earlier US sample in the data, so the onset before 07:49:48Z is unknown.

The Kubernetes cluster readable in this Run is identified by its own Prometheus alert rule labels as cluster: opspilot-m1 (rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, k8s_namespace_name=otel-demo, service_name=checkout, severity critical), and its node is opspilot-m1-control-plane; no object carries the label production-us-east-1.

In that cluster, namespace otel-demo contains Deployment checkout (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and Deployment payment (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment), each with 1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available replica, and pods checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n and payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d both Running and ready; the payment container's env has only PAYMENT_PORT, FLAGD_HOST, FLAGD_PORT and OTel settings, with no Stripe or external payment-provider address, and the only Services matching payment/checkout/stripe are ClusterIP services payment and checkout in otel-demo.

In the readable cluster the payment pod's own logs between 2026-11-22T09:45:49Z and 09:48:54Z show repeated 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' with transactionIds, and the checkout pod's logs in the same period show '[PlaceOrder] ...', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent ...' - so this cluster's checkout-to-payment path was succeeding at the end of the window and does not exhibit the failure recorded for production-us-east-1.

Every otel-demo pod in the readable cluster (22 pods, including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n) shows restartCount 2 and a last termination at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown; kube-state-metrics and prometheus-readonly-proxy instead show lastState reason Error (exit 2 at 08:04:50Z and exit 1 at 08:04:42Z) - a cluster-wide restart rather than a checkout/payment-specific crash.

The fault-injection flags held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config for this workload family were off at query time: paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') both have state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', as do cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, adManualGc and adHighCpu.

No otel-demo Kubernetes object shows a checkout fault during the window: events recorded inside the window exist only for namespace app-101 (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Created/Scheduled/Pulled/Started/Killing) plus two Warning events 'FailedToCreateEndpoint' for endpoints orca (app-95, 09:21:00Z) and signup-service (app-162, 09:32:52Z), and the only namespaces present are app-102 (created 09:51:11Z), default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo.

The checkout failures in production-us-east-1 trace to the external payment provider stripe-us: payment-service's /v1/charges calls to stripe-us exceeded the 30s timeout (08:49:47Z), checkout-service saw the payment provider response time out (07:49:48Z), and the accumulated payment failures then opened checkout's circuit breaker for payment-service at 44% failure rate (09:19:47Z). What is wrong inside stripe-us (latency, errors, throttling) is not observable from any data source in this Run.

Fault injection through the otel-demo flagd flags paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable, or through the readable cluster's checkout/payment deployment configuration, is not supported as the cause of this checkout incident: both payment flags read defaultVariant 'off', the payment deployment carries no external provider address or fault-injection env, and the readable cluster's payment and checkout pods completed transactions normally at 09:45-09:48Z.

The 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z exit-255 termination of every otel-demo pod in the readable cluster (including payment and checkout) is not supported as the cause of the production-us-east-1 checkout errors: it affected all 22 pods uniformly rather than checkout or payment alone, the pods are ready now, their post-restart logs show successful payments, and the readable cluster carries a different identity (cluster: opspilot-m1) than the cluster that logged the failures.

Ask the owner of the stripe-us payment-provider integration to check provider-side latency/error status and the 30s client timeout and circuit-breaker thresholds used by payment-service and checkout-service for the production-us-east-1 deployment, since the recorded failures are all timeout/circuit-breaker paths on that dependency.

Attach the production-us-east-1 cluster itself to the observability target (or confirm which cluster label the readable opspilot-m1 cluster should carry) so that pod status, events and metrics can be checked for the cluster that produced these checkout errors.

gaps: No metrics: every Prometheus call in this Run (get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment latency/error rates, rpc_* and traces_span_metrics values could not be measured; the alert rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh exists in ConfigMap otel-demo/prometheus but its current or historical firing state is unknown.

No traces: traces_list_services, traces_search (checkout, payment) and traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error status, latency or parent-child edge for checkout -> payment -> stripe-us could be confirmed.

No Kubernetes visibility into cluster production-us-east-1: the only readable cluster labels itself cluster: opspilot-m1, has no app-262 namespace, and has no stripe-us workload or Service, so pod status, events, ConfigMaps and Secrets of the failing US cluster could not be inspected.

Onset and end of the production-us-east-1 degradation are unknown: the earliest US sample is 2026-11-22T07:49:48Z and the latest 2026-11-22T09:19:47Z; nothing in the index shows whether failures continued after 09:19:47Z.

stripe-us itself is unobservable: there are no logs, metrics, traces or Kubernetes objects for the payment provider, so provider-side latency, error rate and the reason for the 30s timeouts are unknown.

Why all 22 otel-demo pods in the readable cluster terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exit code 255 (reason Unknown) is unknown: previous container logs were empty (0 bytes read) and no otel-demo event explains it; it is not tied to this checkout incident by any evidence.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment, config or flag change history for the payment provider configuration or the US cluster could be checked.
Secrets cannot be read, so any credential or provider-endpoint value used by payment-service for stripe-us could not be verified.

A networkpolicies query returned status no_data with 0 objects in the readable cluster (an empty result, not proof of absence), so policy-based blocking between checkout and payment could neither be confirmed nor excluded there, and that query says nothing about production-us-east-1.

Log queries filtered by error/timeout/failure patterns against the payment and checkout pods in the readable cluster (19479009-826e-4130-8d9c-14ec26fabfa2-t0:cbe16c49-f2d3-4850-99de-7ddc8435d538, 19479009-826e-4130-8d9c-14ec26fabfa2-t1:e79a08ea-8841-4f41-a1d6-e7dd1fcee3e4, 15145196-e85b-466c-b08d-c0409570abab-t0:f7fea37d-d9a6-4211-9e63-aa9f5ad7302a) returned status no_data: no matching line in the sampled slices, which does not prove nothing happened.

A pod-status query for pods named exactly payment/checkout returned status no_data (d8c9c80e-1a74-4073-998e-784766df5008-t0:54cdfaa2-232d-4e44-ab0b-9a4aba2b6af1); the pod status facts above come from the pod objects actually named payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, and from the full otel-demo pod listing.
next_steps: Check the Stripe-US provider status page, quota/rate-limit notices and the egress path from the US payment-service for the 07:49-09:20Z period.
Obtain payment-service and checkout-service logs plus metrics from cluster production-us-east-1 itself, including payment charge latency/error rate and the circuit-breaker state transitions.
Review the payment-service 30s client timeout and checkout's circuit-breaker failure-rate threshold (44% observed) for whether they are tuned for this provider's latency profile.
Grant or correct observability access for the production-us-east-1 cluster so pod status, events and per-pod logs can be inspected next time.

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
